newsitem.title: USA: Tenneco Q4 hurt by containerboard weakness.
newsitem.headline: Tenneco Q4 hurt by containerboard weakness.

text.p: Tenneco Inc's fourth-quarter margins were hurt by weak containerboard prices, Chief Executive Dana G. Mead told reporters after the release of the company's 1996 results.
That weakness has continued in the first quarter, he said during a teleconference.

The company reported 1996 operating income of $715 million, or $1.67 per share, compared with $712 million, or $1.62, in 1995. But fourth-quarter operating income slipped to $130 million, or $0.18 per share, from $151 million, or $0.21.

"The 1996 results clearly validate the strategy we have pursued in concentrating on our fast-growing, highly profitable automotive parts and specialty packaging businesses," Mead said in the company's statement.

The company said operating income of its auto parts operations increased 25 percent last year, excluding special charges, to record levels, as operating margins increased to 10.5 percent from 9.7 percent in 1995.
Tenneco Automotive's fourth-quarter operating income accelerated 51 percent to $68 million on strong volume and improvements in manufacturing processes, the company said.
Mead told reporters he had hoped for a strengthening in containerboard prices during the fourth quarter, but "my timing was off. (And) I've seen nothing so far" in the first quarter.
Chief Operating Officer Paul T. Stecko, who is also the packaging unit's chief executive, pointed out the businesss "saw a very week second half of December."
He attributed that to Christmas falling in mid-week. He said the company experienced "an appreciable volume rebound" in the first half of January."
